0|00c5a9834b476a138158fb17d576da751727a9f1|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"net: Fix corruption of skb csum field in pskb_expand_head() of net/core/skbuff.c
Make pskb_expand_head() check ip_summed to make sure csum_start is really
csum_start and not csum before adjusting it.
This fixes a bug I encountered using a Sun Quad-Fast Ethernet card and VLANs.
On my configuration
column2: the sunhme driver produces skbs with differing amounts

column1: of headroom on receive depending on the packet size.  See line 2030 of
drivers/net/sunhme.c; packets smaller than RX_COPY_THRESHOLD have 52 bytes
of headroom but packets larger than that cutoff have only 20 bytes.
When these packets reach the VLAN driver
calls skb_cow()
column3: if the packet has less than NET_SKB_PAD (== 32) bytes

column1: of headroom
Then
column2: pskb_expand_head() needs to adjust a lot of offsets into the skb

column1: including csum_start.  Since csum_start is a union with csum
has a valid csum value this will corrupt it
column2: which was the effect I observed.

column1: The sunhme hardware computes receive checksums
column2: so the skbs would be created

column1: by the driver with ip_summed == CHECKSUM_COMPLETE and a valid csum field
then pskb_expand_head() would corrupt the csum field
error"" message later on
column2: for example in icmp_rcv() for pings larger than the

column1: sunhme RX_COPY_THRESHOLD.
On the basis of the comment at the beginning of include/linux/skbuff.h
I believe that the csum_start skb field is only meaningful if ip_csummed is
CSUM_PARTIAL
column2: so this patch makes pskb_expand_head() adjust it only in that

column1: case to avoid corrupting a valid csum value.
